1_resourceJoin: Identity publish: the App node poll publishes the canonical three-field identities (nodeId/status/lastHeartbeatAt) first. Each node gets a loading observation that carries only the same project's previous value, and then setNodesState('success') runs. Resource reads follow, so a hung or failed usage read can never hide identity, status or heartbeat. After publication, identityPublished makes the catch path return without setting the error state.

Join bounds: joinDashboardResources reads the existing scoped GET /v1/projects/{p}/nodes/{n}/resource-usage with encoded path parts. It uses at most 4 workers and at most 64 reads per poll; nodes beyond 64 get an explicit 'cap / unobserved' observation. Each child read has a 4 s deadline plus the existing 10 s poll timeout, and a Promise wrapper settles even when the transport ignores AbortSignal. Workers stop on abort or on a credential change.

Fences: per-node publish requires the same credential, session, scope and applied request, and not aborted except for the poll's own REQUEST_TIMEOUT. Logout and project switch clear the cache and change the session/scope refs. A cached value is reused only when its projectId equals the current project. A superseded background poll's results are dropped by request === nodeAppliedRef. Its remaining reads can continue only within the 4 s per-read and 10 s per-poll budgets, which bounds the overlap.

Validation: checkedDashboardResources enforces a closed outer shape, source execution-kernel, exact nodeId and an RFC3339 calendar-checked stateAsOf, and throws on mismatch. Per row it enforces a closed shape, the res_ ULID pattern, known kind and unit, safe non-negative integers, and that measured implies reserved/spare/observedAt (unmeasured implies all three are null). A malformed or duplicate row is reported as an issue for its own kind (both rows for a duplicate), so valid other dimensions are kept. A dimension with any issue contributes nothing.

Freshness: currentResourceRows uses only measured rows with the requested unit whose stateAsOf and observedAt are within 60 s and no more than 5 s in the future, and excludes any observation with an error. The real recorded inputs have observedAt equal to lastHeartbeatAt (19:47:39.66Z), captured at 19:47:42Z, so they are about 2 s old and fresh. That means the 60 s window will not mark the live CP as stale under normal heartbeats. Previous values stay visible only as an explicit '이전 관측 / stale' row and are never added to current totals. A failed node page shows a stale warning and excludes all totals.

Display: CPU shows as m (500m per node, 1500m total) and memory as binary units (64 MiB per node, 192 MiB total), with offered as the headline plus registered capacity, reserved and spare. The page states these are execution-kernel offered/reserved/spare snapshots, not physical whole-machine capacity, OS utilization, scheduler admission or run permission. Missing GPU/storage show 'unobserved / unshared (does not mean absent hardware)'. OS/address/utilization show as unobserved. Nothing writes observedAt or grants admission.

OS: observedNode maps a missing OS to 'unknown' instead of the former fake 'windows'. CandidateEvaluation.os is the same type, and the placement predicates are unchanged, so a preferred-OS requirement fails closed against unknown. NodeDetail shows the architecture as unobserved for unknown. Other legacy screens print UNKNOWN; I did not demand an unrelated rewrite.
Legacy path: ClusterOverview switches to the canonical view only when nodes carry a resourceObservation, which only the App join sets. Genuinely legacy complete data keeps the existing path.
Render fan-out: one identity publish plus one functional update per node per poll. The App test proves 3 reads per 5 s poll (3, then 9 after 10 s) with the same card and badge elements.
2_gatewayHealth: Header: it fetches /gateway-healthz with cache no-store and credentials omit. It is healthy only when the status is exactly 200, the MIME is exactly application/json and the parsed status is 'ok'. HTML, text, bad JSON and non-200 all become 'degraded'; a transport error becomes 'offline'. Portal /healthz is no longer consulted.

Vite dev and preview proxy: the target is the existing API proxy target with the path rewritten to /healthz. The bypass returns false (Vite responds 404) unless the URL is exactly /gateway-healthz and the method is GET or HEAD, so a query, suffix or other method is rejected. Authorization and Cookie are removed on the proxy request.

deploy/intranet/portal/nginx.conf: an exact location = /gateway-healthz rejects any query with 400 and any method other than GET/HEAD with 403. It proxies to https://control_plane/healthz with proxy_ssl_verify on, the existing CA bundle, SNI and Host cp.sv.lan, the same as the existing /v1 blocks. It blanks Authorization and Cookie, has no proxy_intercept_errors (so the raw upstream status/body/MIME pass through), disables access_log and caching, uses 2 s connect / 4 s read timeouts, and re-includes the security headers plus Cache-Control no-store. Portal location = /healthz is unchanged static liveness.
apps/web/nginx.conf: the same guards, targeting http://control-plane:8080/healthz, which matches that file's existing in-cluster topology.

Root operator adapter: Root's loopback/SSH adapter must add the exact URI-bearing replacement of proxy_pass https://control_plane/healthz; with proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz;, next to its four existing replacements. Without it the header fails closed to degraded/offline and never fabricates health. This is a future Root operator step, not a source TLS bypass, and the author changed no live service.
